title: Apple Stock Jumps After Better-Than-Expected Q1 Earnings
raw_text: Apple Inc. (AAPL) shares rose 3.2% in trading Monday after the company reported fourth-quarter fiscal 2024 earnings that exceeded Wall Street expectations. Revenue came in at $119.6 billion, up 2% year-over-year, while diluted EPS reached $2.18, beating estimates by $0.05. The company attributed strong iPhone and Services segment growth to robust demand in emerging markets. CEO Tim Cook noted in the earnings call that AI-driven features in the latest iOS updates are driving customer retention. Gross margin expanded to 46.1% from 45.9% in the prior year quarter.

title: US CPI Falls to 3.1% YoY in December, Below Fed Target
raw_text: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.2% in December (seasonally adjusted), bringing the year-over-year rate to 3.1%, down from 3.4% in November. This marks the fifth consecutive month of cooling inflation and moves closer to the Federal Reserve's 2% target. Core CPI (excluding food and energy) came in at 3.7% YoY, down from 3.9% in November. Energy prices fell 1.5% during the month, while food prices ticked up 0.1%. The data suggests the Fed's restrictive monetary policy stance is beginning to have the intended disinflation effect without tipping the economy into recession.

title: Gold Prices Hit 3-Year High Amid Geopolitical Tensions
raw_text: Gold futures extended gains Friday, reaching $2,082 per troy ounce, the highest level since November 2021. Risk-off sentiment driven by escalating tensions in the Middle East and concerns over supply chain disruptions pushed investors into traditional safe-haven assets. The U.S. dollar weakened 0.8% against a basket of major currencies, making gold cheaper for international buyers and supporting prices. Central bank purchases remained robust, with emerging market central banks adding an estimated 750 tonnes of gold reserves in 2023. Technical analysts note that a break above $2,100 could trigger fresh buying from momentum funds.

title: Federal Reserve Press Release: Powell Comments on 2024 Policy Path
raw_text: Fed Chair Jerome Powell remarked during a speech at the Economic Club of Washington that the central bank may have completed its rate-hiking cycle and is now considering the timing of future rate cuts. Powell emphasized that "while inflation has come down substantially, it remains somewhat above our 2% target." He noted that the Fed will take a data-dependent approach in 2024, with three rate cuts currently priced into market expectations. Markets interpreted these comments as hawkish relative to recent dovish rhetoric, pushing bond yields higher and equity futures lower in afternoon trading.

title: NVIDIA Announces Next-Gen AI Accelerator, Shipping Q2 2024
raw_text: NVIDIA Corporation unveiled its next-generation H200 AI accelerator, featuring 141 GB of HBM3E memory and up to 1.8 PB/s memory bandwidth—double the prior generation. The company expects volume production by Q2 2024, with early customers including major cloud providers and research institutions. Analysts view this announcement positively as it extends NVIDIA's lead in the competitive AI chip market and supports its data center revenue growth thesis. The announcement bolstered semiconductor-related ETFs, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index rising 1.9% in morning trading. Some investors raised concerns about geopolitical export restrictions potentially limiting sales to Chinese customers.

title: JPMorgan Chase Beats Earnings Expectations, Eyes 2024 Growth
raw_text: JPMorgan Chase & Co. reported fourth-quarter 2023 net income of $12.4 billion on revenue of $40.8 billion, exceeding analyst expectations on both top and bottom lines. CEO Jamie Dimon stated that despite ongoing economic uncertainty, the bank remains well-positioned for profitable growth in 2024. Investment banking revenue surged 32% YoY, driven by increased M&A activity and capital markets strength. However, net interest margin compression and higher credit losses in the credit card portfolio offset some gains. The bank maintained its dividend and announced a new $30 billion share buyback authorization. Stock futures advanced on the positive guidance and capital return program.

title: US Unemployment Rate Holds Steady at 3.7% in December
raw_text: The U.S. unemployment rate remained unchanged at 3.7% in December 2023, as the economy continued to add 216,000 nonfarm payroll jobs during the month—moderating slightly from 227,000 in November. Labor force participation ticked up to 63.0% from 62.8%, suggesting renewed interest in job-seeking. Average hourly earnings rose 0.3% MoM and 4.1% YoY, consistent with cooling but still-above-target wage growth. The report indicates a labor market that remains resilient but is gradually cooling, supporting the Fed's inflation-fighting narrative without evidence of an imminent recession. Market participants view the data as constructive for the "soft landing" scenario.

title: Oil Prices Slip on Demand Concerns Despite OPEC+ Supply Cuts
raw_text: Crude oil futures fell 2.1% to $76.50/barrel despite OPEC+ reaffirming production cuts of 2.2 million barrels per day through the end of Q1 2024. Concerns over Chinese economic growth and potential demand destruction offset supply-side support. The Energy Information Administration reported U.S. crude inventories rose by 3.2 million barrels last week, above the 5-year average. Traders noted that the recent weakness in oil does not yet reflect the potential for spring refining maintenance season to tighten the market. However, geopolitical risks in the Middle East remain a wildcard that could quickly reverse the bearish trend.
